extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and practitioners seeking an overview of U.S. federal Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) and how to participate in notice-and-comment
extracted.subtask_description: A concise overview of what a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking is, the legal basis and procedural steps for issuing one under the Administrative Procedure Act, the mandatory contents of an NPRM, typical comment periods, and implications for public commenters. Useful for people preparing comments or tracking federal rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: "A public notice that is issued by law when a U.S. federal agency wishes to add, remove, or change a rule or regulation" as part of administrative rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to recognize which agency actions require an NPRM and to understand the NPRM's role as the formal vehicle for soliciting public input before finalizing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis: publication under Section 553 of the APA
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies must publish NPRMs under Section 553 of the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory requirement exists so agencies consider input from affected parties; cite Section 553 when assessing whether an agency followed required procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication venue: Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRMs are published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Federal Register to find official NPRMs, their texts, and formal deadlines; publication there is the triggering event for public participation timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard comment period: initial and reply durations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard comment period: 60 days for initial; 30 additional days for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume a 60-day window to submit initial comments unless the NPRM states otherwise; if a reply period is provided, plan for an additional 30 days to respond to others' comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content — time, place, and nature of the proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRM must include the time, place, and nature of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these details to determine the logistical scope of participation (e.g., public hearings) and to anchor any comments to the specific proceeding referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content — authority citation for the action
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRM must include an authority citation for the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor comments to the agency's stated statutory or regulatory authority; challenging or supporting the agency's authority is a primary avenue for legal or policy arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content — description of subjects and proposed regulation terms
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRM must include a description of subjects and proposed regulation terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map your comments directly to the described subjects and the specific regulatory text or terms proposed; specificity increases comment utility to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content — deadline for written comments
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRM must state the deadline for written comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit by the stated deadline; late comments may be disregarded. Note the deadline when planning research anddrafting to ensure timely submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content — methods for public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: NPRM must describe methods for public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified methods (e.g., electronic submission through Regulations.gov, mail, or public hearing attendance); failure to use prescribed methods can affect whether comments are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary procedure — Notice of Inquiry (NOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Inquiry (NOI): comments before proposals are drafted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An NOI solicits early input to inform whether and how a proposal should be drafted; use NOIs to shape the agency's framing before a formal NPRM is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary procedure — Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM): input on potential changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANPRMs seek broader feedback on possible regulatory approaches and can include questions or options; respond with comparative analyses and suggested alternatives when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further NPRM (FNPRM) when substantial changes occur
rubrics_metrics.description: After comments, agencies may issue a Further NPRM (FNPRM) if substantial changes need additional public input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an FNPRM is issued, treat it like a new NPRM: reassess arguments in light of changes and submit focused comments on the substantive revisions proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access: use of Regulations.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal government launched Regulations.gov in 2002 to improve public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and submit comments via Regulations.gov; it centralizes docket materials, public comments, and agency submissions and is the primary tool for electronic participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication for commenters: anchor comments to NPRM elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The required-contents list shows what's mandatory in the NPRM — anchor your comment to the agency's stated authority, the specified subjects, and the deadline. Comments should make explicit how they map to the published proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical checklist for commenters: (1) cite the NPRM docket and specific proposed text or subject, (2) explain how your point relates to the agency's authority and the stated subjects, and (3) ensure submission via the methods and before the deadline. Explicit mapping increases the chance the agency will treat the comment as responsive and part of the administrative record.
